title: A name to fix
briefing: Someone fat-fingered a filename. There is no `rename` command on Linux —
moving a file to a new name in the same place IS renaming.
tips: `mv OLD NEW` moves a file. If NEW is just a different name, that's a rename.
objective: Rename the misspelled reprot.txt to report.txt.
expert_objective: Fix the name: reprot.txt should be report.txt.
hints: There's no rename command — you MOVE the file to the correct name.
`mv <old name> <new name>` in the same directory renames it.
explanation: `mv` moves a file — and moving it to a new name in the same folder is how you rename on Linux. `mv a.txt dir/` moves it into a directory instead; `mv a.txt dir/b.txt` moves and renames at once.
